title: Multi-file greenfield: a persistent todo CLI across modules
prompt:
Build a command-line todo application in this workspace, organized as TWO modules plus a test file.

`store.py` -- a class `TodoStore` that persists todos to a JSON file:
- `__init__(self, path)`: remember the file path; if it exists, load the todos from it, else start empty.
- Each todo is a dict with integer `id` (auto-incrementing from 1, NEVER reused even after deletion), string `text`, boolean `done` (starts False).
- `add(self, text) -> int`: append a new todo, persist, return its id.
- `list(self, include_done=True) -> list`: return todos (all, or only open ones when include_done is False), in insertion order.
- `complete(self, todo_id) -> bool`: mark done and persist; return False if no such id.
- `remove(self, todo_id) -> bool`: delete and persist; return False if no such id.
Every mutation must save to disk immediately so a fresh TodoStore on the same path sees prior state.

`cli.py` -- a function `main(argv, store)` returning an int exit code, plus an `if __name__ == "__main__":` block that builds `TodoStore("todos.json")` and calls `main(sys.argv[1:], store)` then exits with its code. Subcommands:
- `add <text...>`: join the rest as the text, print `added #<id>` to stdout, return 0.
- `list`: print each OPEN todo as `#<id> <text>` (one per line, insertion order), return 0.
- `list --all`: print ALL todos; done ones prefixed with `x ` (e.g. `x #2 buy milk`), open ones as `#<id> <text>`.
- `done <id>`: on success print `done #<id>` (stdout) return 0; if the id is missing print `no such todo` to STDERR and return 1.
- `rm <id>`: on success print `removed #<id>` (stdout) return 0; missing id prints `no such todo` to STDERR and returns 1.
- unknown or missing subcommand: print a usage line to STDERR and return 2.

Also write `test_todo.py` with pytest tests covering: add returns incrementing ids, list hides done items, `--all` shows done items with the `x ` prefix, complete/remove of a missing id returns False, and ids are not reused after removal. Ensure `python -m pytest test_todo.py` passes.
